findings.where: Nav bar (the gummed binding), the logo at top left, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. The arches and the MMM INFRA wordmark are pale yellow on the red-brown binding, not the logo's grey #404040 and blue #0070C0, and 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' is missing. The palette has no place for either logo colour, and the dark binding ground cannot carry the full-colour logo.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brief says the logo stays and is never redrawn. A returning client who knows the blue wordmark would no longer recognise the practice in the nav.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Write to me' note in the left margin (desktop)
findings.fault: This mailto link is the homepage's one action, but it is small script stranded in the margin. It sits partway down between the tagline and the sketch and lines up with nothing. With a squint, the headline, the photo print and the large aqueduct sketch all outweigh it, so it reads as a doodle rather than the way to get in touch.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff who have decided they may want Mark. They look for a contact route next to his name and credentials, and could miss this one.

findings.where: First screen, the hero copy and the missing footer, both widths
findings.fault: The first visit gives no full email address as text, no base country or regions of work, and no word on who the advice is for. The page also ends with no footer, although the palette names one ('Binding: nav, footer'). A reader cannot tell where Mark works or for whom, and cannot copy his address.
findings.who_objects: Procurement staff at a multilateral bank who screen advisors by region and client type, and who often want an address to paste into an internal email.

findings.where: First screen, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.'
findings.fault: A size-of-experience claim has its own line in the hero. It is the one unverifiable boast on a page whose sub-heading already makes a checkable claim (former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group).
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader, who judges advisors by named bodies and roles rather than year counts. It also cuts against Mark's own 'one strong line, no boasts'.

findings.where: The ground across the whole page: the ruled feints and the double margin line (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The ruling on the page ignores its own palette. The feints render as grey-olive lines, not the pale blue 'Feint #93B3D3' shown in the texture swatch. The double margin line is dark brown, not 'Margin red'. The two marks that make a legal pad recognisable are therefore muted, and the texture specimen and the page disagree.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for the lined yellow legal pad. The page reads as generic ruled yellow paper, and the layout round would inherit two conflicting versions of one texture.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel, the timeline table and its notes (desktop and phone); also the article's lecture row
findings.fault: These blocks are set on a tighter line spacing than the 32 px feints, so the printed rules cut through words and descenders. This breaks the texture's own promise that the feints are 'the line spacing of every text block'.
findings.who_objects: Any reader of the table, who finds struck-through lines harder to read. Angélique would also need to know which blocks escape the grid when she adds content.

findings.where: Article specimen, the related-lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process… Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule sits on the baseline of the title's last line and of '2026 · PDF'. It looks like a cramped underline under only part of the title, or like a table border. The bold title is otherwise set like body text, so it is unclear whether the title is a link or how much of the row is clickable.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants the lecture PDF. They have to hover to find out what is a link.

findings.where: Article specimen, the heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop) and the handwritten pull quote (both widths)
findings.fault: Snapping display lines to double feints leaves a full line-height gap inside one heading and inside one quote. On desktop the two-line heading falls apart into what look like two headings, and on phone the three-line quote looks like three separate notes. On phone the same heading is set tight, so like parts are not treated alike across widths.
findings.who_objects: Article readers, who have to reassemble the title. Angélique, whose new post titles would break the same way.

findings.fault: This is a button, but it carries the link's underline. The underline is the signifier reserved for navigation, so it looks like a link that goes somewhere rather than a control that replays the note in place.
findings.who_objects: A visitor or the founder testing the sketch, who expects a link to leave the page. Every other underline on the page means a link.

findings.fault: The first row's last caption line ('ground', 'the stack', 'rules') sits as close to the second row's swatches as to its own. The space between rows is no bigger than the space inside a swatch's group, so the grouping by proximity blurs.
findings.who_objects: The founder or the layout-round designer reading the palette. They can briefly pair a role with the wrong swatch.
